evidence: Mechanism confirmed in the frozen tree, but the framing overstates it. Review identity carries no base: ReviewRun stores only head_sha (products/stamphog/backend/models.py:141-145) and PullRequest has no base_ref/base_sha column at all (models.py:78-115, only head_branch); the sole base_sha use is a live read at review time for the sandbox clone (temporal/activities.py:414, 468, 990-991), never persisted or compared. The inbox dedupe keys on (pull_request, head_sha) excluding SUPERSEDED/FAILED (tasks/tasks.py:1201-1208) and returns 'already_reviewed' on a COMPLETED same-head run (1209-1221) without any base comparison, and the stale-snapshot guard (1189-1197) only bails when the stored clock is strictly newer, so a retargeted PR (newer updated_at) passes it, gets its descriptive fields refreshed by _upsert_pull_request (319-358, no base field), and hits the dedupe. So a lost retarget delivery followed by a receiver refire (review_hog/backend/receivers.py:83-140, fires on any TaskRun output save carrying pr_url) does nothing, and the standing approval is not retracted. Two things cut the severity. First, the retarget IS handled on its normal path: 'edited' + changes.base is detected (tasks.py:835), retracts at every head and supersedes in-flight runs before any skip can return (853-862, 441-479, dismiss with current_head_sha=''), then flows through the full pipeline creating a fresh same-head run; the inbox carve-out admits base_retargeted for bot-authored self-driving PRs (167, 144-216); tested at tests/test_tasks.py:520-556 ('base_retarget_invalidates_and_rereviews', asserts run_count == 2) and documented as the invariant (products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:16, 102). The inbox leg does not cause the approval to stand; it just misses the recovery. Second, the exposure is not new to this PR: a lost retarget delivery leaves the same approval standing on every human PR the webhook path serves, with no recovery at all, so the inbox leg is at baseline, only short of its own stated goal of recovering lost webhooks (docstring tasks.py:1124-1128 promises recovery for a lost synchronize only; test_tasks.py:970-1000 'missed_webhook_head_gets_reviewed'). On the premise: a lost delivery is a single failure, not a double one. The view returns 202 right after .delay() (presentation/webhooks.py:60-63), the task has max_retries=3 (tasks.py:809), GitHub does not auto-redeliver a failed delivery, and no beat reconciles PR state (tasks/schedules.py carries only DAILY_DIGEST_CRONTAB). That is exactly the failure class the inbox leg already designs around for synchronize, so by the code's own standard it is realistic. Reachability is still narrow: it needs a human retargeting a bot-authored self-driving draft (uncommon), that one delivery lost, and a LATER output save on the TaskRun to refire the receiver (opportunistic; pr_url is written at PR-creation time in products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/workflow.py:607-640, later output saves are not guaranteed). The window closes on the next push, reopen, or retarget: dismiss_stale_approvals voids every approval at workflow start (activities.py:266-290) and the skip paths retract on head-changing actions (tasks.py:887-899). Consequence when it hits is not fail-safe (an approval stands over an unreviewed diff on a draft until someone flips it ready), which is why this is real rather than defensive hardening, but the grant itself was legitimate and the retraction was lost upstream, not refused by this code.
notes: Would drop to not-real if the webhook view or GitHub guaranteed delivery (they do not), or if the inbox leg's docstring did not claim lost-webhook recovery as a design goal (it does, for synchronize, so a retarget omission is a genuine gap in that design). Would rise to should_fix if lost pull_request deliveries are observed in production at any meaningful rate, or if retargeting self-driving PRs is part of the inbox flow (e.g. the agent opens against the wrong base). The suggestion as written is wrong in one detail: keying identity on base SHA (pull_request.base.sha) would spawn spurious re-reviews because GitHub advances that value as the base branch moves; store base_ref on PullRequest in _upsert_pull_request, compare the fetched base.ref against it in process_inbox_pr_review before the head dedupe, and on mismatch call _retract_approvals_on_base_retarget and create a new run even at a matching head. Treating a missing stored base_ref on older rows as a mismatch would force one re-review per legacy PR, so seed it on first refresh instead. A sibling gap exists for the webhook leg's own 'edited' payload when the stored clock is newer (it is dropped as stale at tasks.py:1016-1027 after the retraction at 853-862 has already run, so that one is fine).
